vo: This tiger is bright orange. So why can't a deer see it?
We see orange. But deer only have two types of colour cones. To them, orange and green look almost the same.
So in tall grass, this tiger doesn't stand out. To its prey, it almost disappears.
Then the stripes finish the job. They break up its outline, like shadows between the grass.

label: Strange but true
vo: And here's the strange part. Shave a tiger, and its skin is striped too.
No two tigers have the same pattern. Their stripes are as unique as your fingerprints.
So that bright orange coat isn't a mistake.
It's one of the best disguises in nature. Only we see it as orange.
